record.paper_title: String Theory on ADS3: Some Open Questions
record.original_question: How can one define and compute meaningful characters or partition-function ingredients for non-compact SU(1,1) Wess–Zumino–Witten representations when the global representations are infinite-dimensional, the current-algebra modules have infinite degeneracy at each level, and no character formula is available for continuous-series representations?

evidence.quote: The unitary representations of the global algebra being infinite-dimensional, there is an infinite degeneracy level by level in the representations of the current algebra, and consequently the characters (2.3) are ill-defined.
this definition does not allow a regularization of the characters of the representations based on the continuous series.

One is the infinite degeneracy at each level in the representations of the current algebra, and in particular the treatment of the representations based on the continuous series for which no character formula has been proposed in the mathematical literature.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Wess–Zumino–Witten model based on the non-compact group SU(1,1) (equivalently SL(2,R)), whose chiral algebra is the affine current algebra sl(2,R)_k at level k. The unitary representations of the global sl(2,R) algebra include: (i) the highest- and lowest-weight discrete series D_j^± (with j a real Casimir parameter), and (ii) the principal and supplementary continuous series C_j^α (parameterized by j = 1/2 + is, s ∈ R, and a real number α ∈ [0,1)). All these global representations are infinite-dimensional, and the corresponding affine modules have infinite degeneracy at every excitation level, so the naive trace

χ(τ, ν) = Tr( q^{L_0 − c/24} z^{J_0^3} ),  q = e^{2πiτ}, z = e^{2πiν},

is divergent. Moreover, no closed character formula is available for the affine modules built on the continuous-series representations.

Problem. Give a precise definition of characters (or suitable partition-function building blocks) for the affine SU(1,1) modules — including in particular those based on the continuous series — such that:

(a) the resulting objects are well-defined (after a specified regularization or distributional interpretation), 
(b) they admit explicit formulas reproducing the known character formulas for the discrete series in an appropriate limit, 
(c) they transform in a controlled way under the modular group SL(2,Z), and 
(d) they combine into a modular-invariant one-loop torus partition function of the SU(1,1) WZW model consistent with unitarity of the underlying conformal field theory.

Determine such characters explicitly, prove their modular transformation properties, and exhibit a modular-invariant partition function built from them.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was substantially resolved by the Maldacena–Ooguri series "Strings in AdS3 and the SL(2,R) WZW model" (especially Part I, hep-th/0001053, and Part II, hep-th/0005183), which gave a well-defined regularization of SL(2,R) WZW characters, computed the one-loop torus partition function, decomposed it into contributions from discrete and continuous series, and demonstrated modular invariance. Continuous-series characters are interpreted distributionally with a spectral density; subsequent work (e.g., Eguchi–Sugawara on non-holomorphic modular forms for SL(2,R)/U(1)) further clarified modular completions mixing discrete and continuous representations.

status_evidence.title: Strings in AdS3 and the SL(2,R) WZW model. II: Euclidean black hole
status_evidence.snippet: Computes the one-loop partition function of the SL(2,R) WZW model and decomposes it into characters of discrete and continuous representations.
status_evidence.claim: Provides well-defined partition-function ingredients including continuous-series contributions.

status_evidence.title: Non-holomorphic Modular Forms and SL(2,R)/U(1) Superconformal Field Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Discrete characters are accompanied by continuous representations with non-holomorphic coefficients forming Jacobi-like modular objects.
status_evidence.claim: Modular completions involving continuous-series characters are known.
